# Published F100 forward-route witness

This bounded fixture retains the original `mir-fixture-mir5-historical-transition` mod identity and its private `mir5_historical_transition` saved state, rather than creating another predecessor world or borrowing the MIR5-origin laser source. It requires the protected published4.7.10003/1.0.0 source `219EF20F63B4A85FA2386BD50A81228B28F006D9731F24E069A657BB13F45811` and independently rechecks its actual mining lab, consumed science, level2/+5%, frozen lab and42% mining/braking queue before adding witnesses. Original saves and adverse receipts remain unchanged.

Prepare one enhanced copy under published MIR4.7.10003. Seed the seven actual finite `laser-turret-speed-1` through `-7` rows and one inserter continuation level, with exact native effects and2.2 laser/2-and4 inserter totals. The retained F1004.4 native capture establishes these finite definitions and the absence of a published laser8 in that earlier closure; the actual4.7.3 preflight must confirm that absence rather than invent a technology. An unexpected laser8 stops preparation for review. The original actual mining lab is reused once; these additional laser/inserter states are explicitly seeded, not claimed as lab-earned.

The enhanced source snapshots all16 retained F100 MIR rows plus seven finite laser rows, and creates separate27% suspended and42%-queued foreign-disabled witnesses. Both requested destinations consume this same protected enhanced save. Canonical comparison permits only the engine laser-name/ammo and stack-to-bulk token/field mappings, plus one new useful mining level/+10% total. Every row's levels, flags, caps, investment and effect vector remains checked, alongside source-lab state, unrelated forces and the original queue. The successor saves and passes two independent unchanged-byte read-only cold reloads. A completed-successor configuration callback revalidates every assertion instead of importing the source again.

Attempt each requested endpoint directly. Only an actual engine save-format refusal permits the separately declared published4.7.11003/1.1.110 bridge on a disposable copy; that bridge validates and saves preserved state without new research. Never install MIR5 at an intermediate engine or use the MIR5 F110 destination as the F210 origin. Keep DLC, providers and startup settings unchanged. Compose each stage's five files with shared/control.lua as fixture_control.lua and shared/data-final-fixes.lua as fixture_data_final.lua. Black Glass binds exact profiles, own containers, final player hashes and the existing historical process/library helpers before native dispatch; fixture existence and host controls are not native qualification.

Use `tools/Invoke-NativeFixture.ps1 -PublishedF100ForwardStage source|bridge|f110|f210` with the corresponding exact profile, composed fixture and protected `InputSavePath`/hash. This selector reuses existing process/library/resource/save/reload handling, admits no fresh world and excludes all other fixture modes. The prepared source profile pins published C04F and the reproduced own BD39 fixture; the successor profiles must additionally pin the actual enhanced save and final player bytes. The [original prepared input receipt](../../../spec/evidence/published-f100-forward-prepared-aero-r01.json) retains exact original members and the source command; its hash-only bridge assumption is superseded by the separately recorded refusal-body correction.

A future bridge profile requires `engine_bridge_refusal` containing retained `result`, `profile`, `stdout` and `ledger` references, each with actual `path` and uppercase `sha256`, plus `endpoint` with `target`, `mir_sha256` and `fixture_sha256`. The reader rehashes every bounded body and rejects duplicate JSON properties. It matches the direct requested F110 or F210 endpoint, identical enhanced input, exact destination engine, selected MIR/fixture archives and failed native result, then requires a governed process start/interruption and the actual native save-format diagnostic/header. Missing bodies, invented hashes, source/engine/archive/route mismatches, success, timeout, resource errors and unrelated native errors do not authorize a bridge. The usual published F110 bridge follows an actual failed direct F100→F210 attempt; an unrelated F110 result is not a substitute. Unrecognized diagnostic wording stops for review of the preserved actual failure instead of guessing or rerunning until admission succeeds.
